_comment: Base models offered by the MiniMax-H3 Prompt Rewriter node.
This file is yours to edit — add any Qwen3.6-27B build you like and it appears
in the node's model dropdown after a browser refresh. It is copied into the
ComfyUI user directory on first use, so updating the node pack never
overwrites your edits.
Entries added to the pack in later versions ARE merged into your copy, so a
model added after you installed still reaches you. Beside the lists you will
find 'seed_offered': every name the pack has already put in front of this
installation. Anything you delete is recorded there and never comes back;
anything genuinely new is not, and arrives. Delete a name from 'seed_offered'
and that entry will be offered again on the next start. The previous copy of
this file is kept beside it as models.json.bak whenever a merge happens.
The two 'adapters' sections are merged the same way, one format at a time,
and recorded in 'seed_offered' under the section name. So a format published
later - the safetensors build of the 8B adapter, say - arrives in your copy
as a line you can point somewhere else, and one you delete on purpose stays
deleted.
Fields:
name        label shown in the dropdown; keep it stable or saved workflows lose their choice
repo        Hugging Face repository id, or an absolute path to a local folder/file
format      'transformers' (a folder of safetensors) or 'gguf' (one file, run by llama.cpp)
file        gguf only: which file inside the repository to fetch
download_gb approximate download size, shown in the label
vram        short note about what it needs to run, shown in the label
note        optional warning appended to the label
transformers builds are verified from their config.json (4 KB) before anything
is downloaded: wrong architecture, a missing runtime package, or a quantization
PEFT cannot attach a LoRA to are all reported up front.
gguf builds need llama-cpp-python installed, and use the GGUF adapter below
rather than the PEFT one. They are the low-VRAM route: a Q4_K_M base is 15.7 GB
instead of 52 GB, and the IQ2/IQ3 quants go lower still at some quality cost.
The adapter itself also comes in two sizes. 'file' is what is fetched by default,
and everything under 'alternatives' is offered beside it in the options node's
'adapter' dropdown and downloaded from the same repository when picked. Q8_0 is
1.85 GB against F16's 3.48 GB and still produces the trained cut-point form, so
it is the better choice on a card that is tight for room.
'models_8b' and 'adapters_8b' are the second rewriter: a much smaller model that
is multimodal, so it reads the first and last frame itself instead of a caption
of them. Separate lists because the two take different architectures - an entry
from one will not load in the other's node, and offering it there would only
produce a tensor-shape error after a multi-gigabyte download. Same fields, and
the base needs an 'mmproj' for the same reason a captioner does - while a 'transformers' base is one folder and needs none.
'writers' is a separate list, for the guided writer nodes. Those carry the H3
format in the system prompt instead of in a LoRA, so any instruction-following
GGUF works and nothing here has to be Qwen3.6-27B. Same fields, gguf only.
Every GGUF already in your ComfyUI model folders is offered there too.
'captioners' is the list for the reference captioner node, which describes an
image, an audio clip or a video so the Ref2VA writer knows what is in it. Those
entries need one extra field, 'mmproj': a multimodal model is two files and
both come from the same conversion.
Be careful adding to it. Publishing a GGUF plus an mmproj is not the same as
llama.cpp's mtmd being able to load them: gemma-4's projector, for one, aborts
the process outright on b10310 with both Google's and unsloth's files. Every
entry below has actually been run. A local folder holding a model and its
mmproj side by side is offered automatically, so you can try one without
editing anything here.

writers.note: best writing per gigabyte; lower gpu_layers if 8 GB is tight

writers.vram: ~10 GB with the guide in context

writers.name: Mistral Small 3.2 24B Instruct
writers.vram: ~17 GB with the guide in context
writers.note: for a 16 GB card and up, when the 9B's prose is not enough

writers.name: Qwen3.8-27B Q2_K_XL
writers.vram: ~13 GB with the guide in context
writers.note: the 27B's prose on a 16 GB card; unsloth's dynamic 2-bit, rougher than the Q4 but still the biggest writer this side of it

writers.name: Qwen3.8-27B Q3_K_XL
writers.vram: ~16 GB with the guide in context
writers.note: the middle road: most of the Q4's quality, three gigabytes less to hold

writers.name: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M
writers.vram: ~19 GB with the guide in context
writers.note: the strongest prose in the list, for a 24 GB card; newer than the rewriter's own base, but its extra layer is why the 27B LoRA cannot ride it

writers.name: Qwen3.8-27B Q6_K_XL
writers.vram: ~27 GB with the guide in context
writers.note: near-lossless, for a 32 GB card - and little room for the video model beside it; lower gpu_layers if it will not fit

captioners.name: Qwen2.5-Omni-3B
captioners.note: image, audio and video in one small model; verified against this pack

captioners.name: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B
captioners.note: same modalities, better prose; step up when the 3B's captions are too plain
